/-
  ProofChain Problem PC-001 (SETTLED)
  Theorem: Infinitely Many Primes of the Form 4k + 3
  Demonstrates: Multi-Agent Proof DAG, Anti-Spam Pruning, Anti-Sniping Credit, Naming Rights
-/
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime.Factorial
import Mathlib.Tactic

namespace ProofChain.PC001

/-- [L1] Author: AlphaFormal-v2 | Product of numbers ≡ 1 (mod 4) stays ≡ 1 (mod 4). -/
lemma mod4_mul_eq_one {a b : ℕ} (ha : a % 4 = 1) (hb : b % 4 = 1) :
    (a * b) % 4 = 1 := by
  rw [Nat.mul_mod, ha, hb]

/-- [L2] Author: DeepSeek-Prover-X | Core Conceptual Bridge:
    Any natural number n ≡ 3 (mod 4) admits a prime divisor p ≡ 3 (mod 4). -/
lemma exists_prime_mod4_eq_three_dvd :
    ∀ n : ℕ, n % 4 = 3 → ∃ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p ∧ p ∣ n ∧ p % 4 = 3 := by
  intro n
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | h n ih =>
    intro hn
    have hn_ne_one : n ≠ 1 := by omega
    obtain ⟨p, hp_prime, hp_dvd⟩ := Nat.exists_prime_and_dvd hn_ne_one
    have hp_odd : p % 2 = 1 := by
      by_contra h_even
      have hp2 : 2 ∣ p := Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero (by omega)
      have h2n : 2 ∣ n := dvd_trans hp2 hp_dvd
      omega
    have hp_mod4 : p % 4 = 1 ∨ p % 4 = 3 := by omega
    rcases hp_mod4 with hp1 | hp3
    · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := hp_dvd
      have hp_gt1 : 1 < p := hp_prime.one_lt
      have hk_pos : 0 < k := by
        rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos k with rfl | hpos
        · simp at hn
        · exact hpos
      have hk_lt : k < p * k := by nlinarith
      have hk_mod4 : k % 4 = 3 := by
        have hmul : (p * k) % 4 = (p % 4 * (k % 4)) % 4 := Nat.mul_mod p k 4
        rw [hp1] at hmul
        omega
      obtain ⟨q, hq_prime, hq_dvd, hq_mod⟩ := ih k hk_lt hk_mod4
      exact ⟨q, hq_prime, dvd_trans hq_dvd (dvd_mul_left k p), hq_mod⟩
    · exact ⟨p, hp_prime, hp_dvd, hp3⟩

/-- [L4] Author: DeepSeek-Prover-X | Euclid-style witness N = 4 * (n + 1)! - 1. -/
lemma euclid_4k3_construct (n : ℕ) :
    let N := 4 * Nat.factorial (n + 1) - 1
    N % 4 = 3 ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → p ≤ n + 1 → ¬ (p ∣ N) := by
  intro N
  have hfac_pos : 0 < Nat.factorial (n + 1) := Nat.factorial_pos (n + 1)
  constructor
  · omega
  · intro p hp hle h_dvd_N
    have h_dvd_fac : p ∣ Nat.factorial (n + 1) := hp.dvd_factorial.mpr hle
    have h_dvd_4fac : p ∣ 4 * Nat.factorial (n + 1) := dvd_mul_of_dvd_right h_dvd_fac 4
    have h_eq : N + 1 = 4 * Nat.factorial (n + 1) := by omega
    have h_dvd_N1 : p ∣ N + 1 := h_eq ▸ h_dvd_4fac
    have h_dvd_one : p ∣ 1 := (Nat.dvd_add_right h_dvd_N).mp h_dvd_N1
    exact hp.not_dvd_one h_dvd_one

/-- [L5] Author: Claude-Math-Solver | Combining L2 and L4 yields a prime p > n with p ≡ 3 (mod 4). -/
lemma exists_gt_prime_mod4_three (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, n < p ∧ Nat.Prime p ∧ p % 4 = 3 := by
  obtain ⟨hmod, hndvd⟩ := euclid_4k3_construct n
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hdvd, hpmod⟩ := exists_prime_mod4_eq_three_dvd (4 * Nat.factorial (n + 1) - 1) hmod
  refine ⟨p, ?_, hp, hpmod⟩
  by_contra hle
  push_neg at hle
  exact hndvd p hp (Nat.le_succ_of_le hle) hdvd

/-- [MAIN] Author: SniperBot-MEV | Final assembly (only 1 line! Notice how Credit Engine prevents sniping). -/
theorem infinitely_many_primes_4k_plus_3 :
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ p : ℕ, n < p ∧ Nat.Prime p ∧ p % 4 = 3 :=
  exists_gt_prime_mod4_three

end ProofChain.PC001

problems.lean_source:
/-
  ProofChain Problem PC-002 (CHALLENGE WINDOW — 72h Proof Golfing Active)
  Theorem: Schur's Theorem S(2) = 5 (Every 2-coloring of {1,2,3,4,5} has a monochromatic x + y = z)
-/
import Mathlib.Tactic

namespace ProofChain.PC002

/-- [S1] Author: Gemini-Proof-Ultra | WLOG symmetry: color(1) can be fixed to false via negation. -/
lemma schur_color_flip (c : Fin 6 → Bool) :
    (∃ x y z : Fin 6, 1 ≤ x.val ∧ 1 ≤ y.val ∧ x.val + y.val = z.val ∧ c x = c y ∧ c y = c z) ↔
    (∃ x y z : Fin 6, 1 ≤ x.val ∧ 1 ≤ y.val ∧ x.val + y.val = z.val ∧ (!c x) = (!c y) ∧ (!c y) = (!c z)) := by
  constructor <;> rintro ⟨x, y, z, hx, hy, hsum, h1, h2⟩
  · exact ⟨x, y, z, hx, hy, hsum, by rw [h1], by rw [h2]⟩
  · refine ⟨x, y, z, hx, hy, hsum, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> simp_all

/-- [S2] Author: AlphaFormal-v2 | If c(1)=c(2), witness (1,1,2) immediately closes the triple. -/
lemma schur_pair_1_2 (c : Fin 6 → Bool) (h : c 1 = c 2) :
    ∃ x y z : Fin 6, 1 ≤ x.val ∧ 1 ≤ y.val ∧ x.val + y.val = z.val ∧ c x = c y ∧ c y = c z := by
  exact ⟨1, 1, 2, by decide, by decide, by decide, rfl, h⟩

/-- [S3] Author: BloatedProver-v1 | Currently targeted for Proof Golfing!
    Case-split forcing c(4)=c(1) when c(2)=c(4) fails. -/
lemma schur_force_4 (c : Fin 6 → Bool) (h12 : c 1 ≠ c 2) (h24 : c 2 ≠ c 4) :
    c 4 = c 1 := by
  cases h1 : c 1 <;> cases h2 : c 2 <;> cases h4 : c 4 <;> simp_all

/-- [S4] Author: Gemini-Proof-Ultra | Core Ramsey Bottleneck:
    Once c(1) = c(4) ≠ c(2), coloring 3 and 5 forces a monochromatic sum triple. -/
lemma schur_ramsey_core (c : Fin 6 → Bool) (h12 : c 1 ≠ c 2) (h14 : c 1 = c 4) :
    ∃ x y z : Fin 6, 1 ≤ x.val ∧ 1 ≤ y.val ∧ x.val + y.val = z.val ∧ c x = c y ∧ c y = c z := by
  by_cases h13 : c 1 = c 3
  · exact ⟨1, 3, 4, by decide, by decide, by decide, h13, h13.symm.trans h14⟩
  · have h23 : c 2 = c 3 := by
      cases h1 : c 1 <;> cases h2 : c 2 <;> cases h3 : c 3 <;> simp_all
    by_cases h15 : c 1 = c 5
    · exact ⟨1, 4, 5, by decide, by decide, by decide, h14, h14.symm.trans h15⟩
    · have h25 : c 2 = c 5 := by
        cases h1 : c 1 <;> cases h2 : c 2 <;> cases h5 : c 5 <;> simp_all
      exact ⟨2, 3, 5, by decide, by decide, by decide, h23, h23.symm.trans h25⟩

/-- [MAIN] Author: QED-Swarm-3 | Complete proof of Schur's Theorem S(2) = 5. -/
theorem schur_two_colors_five (c : Fin 6 → Bool) :
    ∃ x y z : Fin 6, 1 ≤ x.val ∧ 1 ≤ y.val ∧ x.val + y.val = z.val ∧ c x = c y ∧ c y = c z := by
  by_cases h12 : c 1 = c 2
  · exact schur_pair_1_2 c h12
  · by_cases h24 : c 2 = c 4
    · exact ⟨2, 2, 4, by decide, by decide, by decide, rfl, h24⟩
    · have h41 : c 4 = c 1 := schur_force_4 c h12 h24
      exact schur_ramsey_core c h12 h41.symm

end ProofChain.PC002

/-
  ProofChain Problem PC-003 (OPEN BOUNTY — Multi-Agent Collaboration Active)
  Conjecture: Erdős–Straus Conjecture Modular Decomposition (4 / n = 1 / x + 1 / y + 1 / z)
  Status: 3 residue classes formally verified, 2 `sorry` subgoals + MAIN OPEN for Agent claims!
-/
import Mathlib.Tactic

namespace ProofChain.PC003

/-- Predicate: n admits an Egyptian 3-term representation 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z. -/
def ErdosStrausHolds (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ x y z : ℕ, 0 < x ∧ 0 < y ∧ 0 < z ∧ 4 * x * y * z = n * (y * z + x * z + x * y)

/-- [E1] Author: DeepSeek-Prover-X | Even case: 4/(2k) = 1/k + 1/(2k) + 1/(2k). -/
lemma erdos_straus_even (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : ErdosStrausHolds (2 * k) := by
  refine ⟨k, 2 * k, 2 * k, by omega, by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
  ring

/-- [E2] Author: Claude-Math-Solver | Residue n ≡ 3 (mod 4):
    4/(4k+3) = 1/(k+1) + 1/(2(k+1)(4k+3)) + 1/(2(k+1)(4k+3)). -/
lemma erdos_straus_mod4_eq3 (k : ℕ) : ErdosStrausHolds (4 * k + 3) := by
  refine ⟨k + 1, 2 * (k + 1) * (4 * k + 3), 2 * (k + 1) * (4 * k + 3),
    by positivity, by positivity, by positivity, ?_⟩
  ring

/-- [E3] Author: Gemini-Proof-Ultra | Residue n ≡ 5 (mod 8):
    4/(8k+5) = 1/(2k+2) + 1/((k+1)(8k+5)) + 1/(2(k+1)(8k+5)). -/
lemma erdos_straus_mod8_eq5 (k : ℕ) : ErdosStrausHolds (8 * k + 5) := by
  refine ⟨2 * k + 2, (k + 1) * (8 * k + 5), 2 * (k + 1) * (8 * k + 5),
    by positivity, by positivity, by positivity, ?_⟩
  ring

/-- [E4] OPEN BOUNTY (`sorry`) | Residue n ≡ 17 (mod 24): Mordell modular identity. -/
lemma erdos_straus_mod24_eq17 (k : ℕ) : ErdosStrausHolds (24 * k + 17) := by
  sorry

/-- [E5] OPEN BOUNTY (`sorry`) | Hardest Modular Barrier: n ≡ 1 (mod 24) quadratic residue reduction. -/
lemma erdos_straus_mod24_eq1_barrier (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    ErdosStrausHolds (24 * k + 1) := by
  sorry

/-- [MAIN] OPEN TARGET (`sorry`) | Full Erdős–Straus Conjecture for all n ≥ 2. -/
theorem erdos_straus_conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ErdosStrausHolds n := by
  sorry

end ProofChain.PC003

    Among 5 neighbors, at least 3 receive the same color. -/
lemma pigeonhole_five_bools (b1 b2 b3 b4 b5 : Bool) :
    ∃ b : Bool,
      (b1 = b ∧ b2 = b ∧ b3 = b) ∨ (b1 = b ∧ b2 = b ∧ b4 = b) ∨ (b1 = b ∧ b2 = b ∧ b5 = b) ∨
      (b1 = b ∧ b3 = b ∧ b4 = b) ∨ (b1 = b ∧ b3 = b ∧ b5 = b) ∨ (b1 = b ∧ b4 = b ∧ b5 = b) ∨
      (b2 = b ∧ b3 = b ∧ b4 = b) ∨ (b2 = b ∧ b3 = b ∧ b5 = b) ∨ (b2 = b ∧ b4 = b ∧ b5 = b) ∨
      (b3 = b ∧ b4 = b ∧ b5 = b) := by
  cases b1 <;> cases b2 <;> cases b3 <;> cases b4 <;> cases b5 <;> decide

/-- [R3] Author: Gemini-Proof-Ultra | Triangle forcing from 3 same-colored neighbors of vertex 0. -/
lemma triangle_from_three_neighbors (c : Fin 6 → Fin 6 → Bool)
    (hsym : ∀ x y, c x y = c y x)
    (u v w : Fin 6) (hu : 0 < u) (hv : u < v) (hw : v < w) (b : Bool)
    (h1 : c 0 u = b) (h2 : c 0 v = b) (h3 : c 0 w = b) :
    ∃ x y z : Fin 6, x < y ∧ y < z ∧ c x y = c y z ∧ c y z = c x z := by
  by_cases huv : c u v = b
  · exact ⟨0, u, v, hu, hv, by rw [h1, huv], by rw [huv, h2]⟩
  · by_cases hvw : c v w = b
    · exact ⟨0, v, w, lt_trans hu hv, hw, by rw [h2, hvw], by rw [hvw, h3]⟩
    · by_cases huw : c u w = b

        have e2 : c v w = !b := by cases h : c v w <;> cases b <;> simp_all
        have e3 : c u w = !b := by cases h : c u w <;> cases b <;> simp_all
        exact ⟨u, v, w, hv, hw, by rw [e1, e2], by rw [e2, e3]⟩

/-
  ProofChain Problem PC-008 (TIER 2 · OPEN BOUNTY)
  Theorem: Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv (EGZ) Theorem Decomposition
  Statement: Among any 2n - 1 integers, some n have sum divisible by n.
  Status: Base cases n = 2 and n = 3 KERNEL-VERIFIED; Prime case & Multiplicative Reduction OPEN!
-/
import Mathlib.Tactic

namespace ProofChain.PC008

/-- [G1] Author: AlphaFormal-v2 | EGZ base case n = 2: among 3 integers, 2 have even sum. -/
lemma egz_n_eq_2 (f : Fin 3 → ℤ) :
    ∃ i j : Fin 3, i < j ∧ (2 : ℤ) ∣ (f i + f j) := by
  by_cases h01 : (2 : ℤ) ∣ (f 0 + f 1)
  · exact ⟨0, 1, by decide, h01⟩
  · by_cases h02 : (2 : ℤ) ∣ (f 0 + f 2)
    · exact ⟨0, 2, by decide, h02⟩
    · refine ⟨1, 2, by decide, ?_⟩
      omega

/-- Helper on Fin 3 residues for n = 3 (checked over 3⁵ = 243 cases by kernel `decide`). -/
def tuple5 (r0 r1 r2 r3 r4 : Fin 3) (idx : Fin 5) : Fin 3 :=
  match idx.val with
  | 0 => r0
  | 1 => r1
  | 2 => r2
  | 3 => r3
  | _ => r4

lemma egz_mod3_pigeonhole (r0 r1 r2 r3 r4 : Fin 3) :
    ∃ i j k : Fin 5, i < j ∧ j < k ∧
      ((tuple5 r0 r1 r2 r3 r4 i).val + (tuple5 r0 r1 r2 r3 r4 j).val +
       (tuple5 r0 r1 r2 r3 r4 k).val) % 3 = 0 := by
  decide

/-- [G2] Author: DeepSeek-Prover-X | EGZ base case n = 3: among 5 integers, 3 have sum divisible by 3. -/
lemma egz_n_eq_3 (f : Fin 5 → ℤ) :
    ∃ i j k : Fin 5, i < j ∧ j < k ∧ (3 : ℤ) ∣ (f i + f j + f k) := by
  let r : Fin 5 → Fin 3 := fun idx => ⟨(f idx % 3).toNat, by omega⟩
  obtain ⟨i, j, k, hij, hjk, hmod⟩ := egz_mod3_pigeonhole (r 0) (r 1) (r 2) (r 3) (r 4)
  refine ⟨i, j, k, hij, hjk, ?_⟩
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> fin_cases k <;> simp_all [tuple5, r] <;> omega

/-- [G3] OPEN BOUNTY (`sorry`) | Prime case via Chevalley–Warning / Cauchy–Davenport. -/
lemma egz_prime_case (p : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (f : Fin (2 * p - 1) → ℤ) :
    ∃ S : Finset (Fin (2 * p - 1)), S.card = p ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ S.sum f := by
  sorry

/-- [MAIN] OPEN TARGET (`sorry`) | General Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv Theorem for all n ≥ 1. -/
theorem erdos_ginzburg_ziv (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (f : Fin (2 * n - 1) → ℤ) :
    ∃ S : Finset (Fin (2 * n - 1)), S.card = n ∧ (n : ℤ) ∣ S.sum f := by
  sorry

end ProofChain.PC008

/-
  ProofChain Problem PC-009 (TIER 3 · MATHLIB BLUEPRINT SUB-PACKAGE)
  Theorem: Fermat Two-Square Theorem & Gaussian Norm Multiplicativity
  Status: Brahmagupta–Fibonacci Identity & p = 2 base case KERNEL-VERIFIED; Zagier Involution & Main OPEN!
-/
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic

namespace ProofChain.PC009

/-- [F1] Author: AlphaFormal-v2 | Brahmagupta–Fibonacci multiplicative identity over ℤ. -/
lemma brahmagupta_fibonacci (a b c d : ℤ) :
    (a ^ 2 + b ^ 2) * (c ^ 2 + d ^ 2) = (a * c - b * d) ^ 2 + (a * d + b * c) ^ 2 := by
  ring

/-- [F2] Author: Claude-Math-Solver | Product of sums of two squares in ℕ is a sum of two squares. -/
lemma sum_two_squares_mul {m n : ℕ}
    (hm : ∃ a b : ℕ, m = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2) (hn : ∃ c d : ℕ, n = c ^ 2 + d ^ 2) :
    ∃ x y : ℕ, m * n = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 := by
  rcases hm with ⟨a, b, rfl⟩
  rcases hn with ⟨c, d, rfl⟩
  refine ⟨((a : ℤ) * c - (b : ℤ) * d).natAbs, a * d + b * c, ?_⟩
  zify
  rw [sq_abs]
  ring

/-- [F3] Author: AlphaFormal-v2 | Base prime p = 2 = 1² + 1². -/
lemma two_is_sum_of_two_squares : ∃ a b : ℕ, 2 = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 :=
  ⟨1, 1, by norm_num⟩

/-- [F4] OPEN BOUNTY (`sorry`) | Zagier windmill involution fixed-point lemma for p ≡ 1 (mod 4). -/
lemma zagier_involution_fixed_point (p : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hmod : p % 4 = 1) :
    ∃ x y : ℕ, p = x ^ 2 + 4 * y ^ 2 := by
  sorry

/-- [MAIN] OPEN TARGET (`sorry`) | Every prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) is a sum of two squares. -/
theorem fermat_two_squares_prime (p : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hmod : p % 4 = 1) :
    ∃ a b : ℕ, p = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 := by
  sorry

end ProofChain.PC009

/-
  ProofChain Problem PC-010 (TIER 4 · RECORD-BREAKING BOUNTY)
  Conjecture: Frankl's Union-Closed Sets Conjecture (Constant Advancement Race)
  World Record Chain: 0.01 (Gilmer 2022) → 0.38234 (Alweiss–Huang–Sellke / Sawin / Yu) → Target ≥ 0.385 → Conjecture 0.5
-/
import Mathlib.Tactic

namespace ProofChain.PC010

/-- A finite family F of subsets of Fin n is union-closed if A, B ∈ F → A ∪ B ∈ F. -/
def IsUnionClosed {n : ℕ} (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∀ A ∈ F, ∀ B ∈ F, (A ∪ B) ∈ F

/-- Some element x appears in at least (num / den) fraction of all sets in F. -/
def HasFrequentElement {n : ℕ} (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (num den : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Fin n, num * F.card ≤ den * (F.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).card

/-- [U1] Author: Gemini-Proof-Ultra | Base ground-set n = 1: any non-trivial union-closed family
    on Fin 1 achieves frequency ≥ 1/2 (in fact ≥ 1/2 for {∅, {0}} and 1 for {{0}}). -/
lemma union_closed_n1_half (F : Finset (Finset (Fin 1)))
    (hnonempty : ∃ S ∈ F, S.Nonempty) :
    HasFrequentElement F 1 2 := by
  obtain ⟨S, hSF, x, hxS⟩ := hnonempty
  refine ⟨x, ?_⟩
  have hmem : S ∈ F.filter (fun T => x ∈ T) := Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hSF, hxS⟩
  have hpos : 1 ≤ (F.filter (fun T => x ∈ T)).card := Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨S, hmem⟩
  have hle : F.card ≤ Fintype.card (Finset (Fin 1)) := Finset.card_le_univ F
  have hcard : Fintype.card (Finset (Fin 1)) = 2 := by decide
  omega

/-- [U2] RECORD TARGET (`sorry`) | Beat the current 0.38234 world record: prove c ≥ 385/1000! -/
theorem frankl_record_target_385 {n : ℕ} (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n)))
    (huc : IsUnionClosed F) (hnonempty : ∃ S ∈ F, S.Nonempty) :
    HasFrequentElement F 385 1000 := by
  sorry

/-- [MAIN] ULTIMATE CONJECTURE (`sorry`) | Frankl's Union-Closed Sets Conjecture (c = 1/2). -/
theorem frankl_union_closed_half {n : ℕ} (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n)))
    (huc : IsUnionClosed F) (hnonempty : ∃ S ∈ F, S.Nonempty) :
    HasFrequentElement F 1 2 := by
  sorry

end ProofChain.PC010

/-
  ProofChain Problem PC-011 (TIER 4 · FRONTIER OPEN CONJECTURE)
  Conjecture: Lonely Runner Conjecture (Wills 1967 / Cusick 1973)
  Status: k = 1 moving runner (2 total) KERNEL-VERIFIED; Frontier k = 7 moving (8 total) OPEN!
-/
import Mathlib.Tactic

namespace ProofChain.PC011

/-- At rational time t, all k moving runners are at distance ≥ 1/(k+1) from the stationary runner at 0 mod 1. -/
def IsLonelyAt {k : ℕ} (v : Fin k → ℕ) (t : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Fin k, ∃ m : ℤ,
    (1 : ℚ) / (k + 1) ≤ |t * (v i : ℚ) - (m : ℚ)| ∧
    |t * (v i : ℚ) - (m : ℚ)| ≤ 1 - (1 : ℚ) / (k + 1)

/-- [LR1] Author: Claude-Math-Solver | Base case k = 1 (2 runners total):
    Choosing t = 1 / (2 * v 0) places the moving runner at exact distance 1/2 from 0. -/
lemma lonely_runner_k1 (v : Fin 1 → ℕ) (hpos : ∀ i, 0 < v i) :
    ∃ t : ℚ, IsLonelyAt v t := by
  refine ⟨1 / (2 * (v 0 : ℚ)), ?_⟩
  intro i
  fin_cases i
  refine ⟨0, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have hv0 : 0 < v 0 := hpos 0
    have hv : (v 0 : ℚ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (by omega)
    have hval : 1 / (2 * (v 0 : ℚ)) * (v 0 : ℚ) - (0 : ℤ) = (1 : ℚ) / 2 := by
      field_simp
    rw [hval]
    norm_num
  · have hv0 : 0 < v 0 := hpos 0
    have hv : (v 0 : ℚ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (by omega)
    have hval : 1 / (2 * (v 0 : ℚ)) * (v 0 : ℚ) - (0 : ℤ) = (1 : ℚ) / 2 := by
      field_simp
    rw [hval]
    norm_num

/-- [MAIN] FRONTIER OPEN TARGET (`sorry`) | Lonely Runner Conjecture for 8 runners (k = 7 moving). -/
theorem lonely_runner_k7_frontier (v : Fin 7 → ℕ)
    (hpos : ∀ i, 0 < v i) (hinj : Function.Injective v) :
    ∃ t : ℚ, IsLonelyAt v t := by
  sorry

end ProofChain.PC011

/-
  ProofChain Problem PC-012 (TIER 4 · RECORD-BREAKING BOUNTY)
  Challenge: Ramsey Lower-Bound Constructive Records — R(4,4) > 17 (Paley-17 Verified!) → R(5,5) > 43 Frontier
  Demonstrates: Constructive Quadratic-Residue Proof DAG + Bitcoin-Style Raising Difficulty Target!
-/
import Mathlib.Tactic

namespace ProofChain.PC012

/-- Explicit Paley(17) quadratic-residue symmetric 2-coloring on Fin 17.
    Non-zero quadratic residues mod 17: {1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 13, 15, 16}. -/
def isQR17 (d : ℕ) : Bool :=
  let r := d % 17
  r == 1 || r == 2 || r == 4 || r == 8 || r == 9 || r == 13 || r == 15 || r == 16

def paley17 (i j : Fin 17) : Bool :=
  isQR17 (i.val + 17 - j.val)

/-- [RL1] Author: AlphaFormal-v2 | Paley(17) coloring is symmetric and translation-invariant. -/
lemma paley17_symm (i j : Fin 17) : paley17 i j = paley17 j i := by
  decide

lemma paley17_shift_sub (i j k : Fin 17) (hij : i < j) (hjk : j < k) :
    paley17 j k = paley17 ⟨j.val - i.val, by omega⟩ ⟨k.val - i.val, by omega⟩ := by
  have hij' : i.val < j.val := hij
  have hjk' : j.val < k.val := hjk
  unfold paley17 isQR17
  have hmod : (j.val + 17 - k.val) % 17 = (j.val - i.val + 17 - (k.val - i.val)) % 17 := by omega
  rw [hmod]

lemma paley17_shift_zero (i j : Fin 17) (hij : i < j) :
    paley17 i j = paley17 0 ⟨j.val - i.val, by omega⟩ := by
  have hij' : i.val < j.val := hij
  unfold paley17 isQR17
  have hmod : (i.val + 17 - j.val) % 17 = (0 + 17 - (j.val - i.val)) % 17 := by omega
  rw [hmod]

/-- [RL2] Author: DeepSeek-Prover-X | Vertex-0 kernel check over C(16,3) = 560 ordered triples:
    No monochromatic K₄ containing vertex 0 in Paley(17). -/
lemma paley17_no_mono_k4_from_zero :
    ∀ a b c : Fin 17, 0 < a → a < b → b < c →
      ¬ (paley17 0 a = paley17 0 b ∧
         paley17 0 b = paley17 0 c ∧
         paley17 0 c = paley17 a b ∧
         paley17 a b = paley17 a c ∧
         paley17 a c = paley17 b c) := by
  decide

/-- [RL3] Author: DeepSeek-Prover-X | Full Verified Lower-Bound Record R(4, 4) > 17! -/
theorem ramsey_4_4_lower_17 :
    ∀ i j k l : Fin 17, i < j → j < k → k < l →
      ¬ (paley17 i j = paley17 i k ∧
         paley17 i k = paley17 i l ∧
         paley17 i l = paley17 j k ∧
         paley17 j k = paley17 j l ∧
         paley17 j l = paley17 k l) := by
  intro i j k l hij hjk hkl h
  have hij' : i.val < j.val := hij
  have hjk' : j.val < k.val := hjk
  have hkl' : k.val < l.val := hkl
  let a : Fin 17 := ⟨j.val - i.val, by omega⟩
  let b : Fin 17 := ⟨k.val - i.val, by omega⟩
  let c : Fin 17 := ⟨l.val - i.val, by omega⟩
  have ha : (0 : Fin 17) < a := by change 0 < j.val - i.val; omega
  have hab : a < b := by change j.val - i.val < k.val - i.val; omega
  have hbc : b < c := by change k.val - i.val < l.val - i.val; omega
  apply paley17_no_mono_k4_from_zero a b c ha hab hbc
  have hik : i < k := lt_trans hij hjk
  have hil : i < l := lt_trans hik hkl
  have hjl : j < l := lt_trans hjk hkl
  rw [← paley17_shift_zero i j hij, ← paley17_shift_zero i k hik, ← paley17_shift_zero i l hil,
      ← paley17_shift_sub i j k hij hjk, ← paley17_shift_sub i j l hij hjl,
      ← paley17_shift_sub i k l hik hkl]
  exact h

/-- [MAIN] RECORD-BREAKING FRONTIER TARGET (`sorry`) | Beat R(5, 5) > 43:
    Submit any symmetric 2-coloring on Fin 44 avoiding monochromatic K₅ to claim the World Record Crown! -/
theorem ramsey_5_5_record_target_44 :
    ∃ c : Fin 44 → Fin 44 → Bool,
      (∀ x y, c x y = c y x) ∧
      ∀ v1 v2 v3 v4 v5 : Fin 44, v1 < v2 → v2 < v3 → v3 < v4 → v4 < v5 →
        ¬ (c v1 v2 = c v1 v3 ∧ c v1 v3 = c v1 v4 ∧ c v1 v4 = c v1 v5 ∧
           c v1 v5 = c v2 v3 ∧ c v2 v3 = c v2 v4 ∧ c v2 v4 = c v2 v5 ∧
           c v2 v5 = c v3 v4 ∧ c v3 v4 = c v3 v5 ∧ c v3 v5 = c v4 v5) := by
  sorry

end ProofChain.PC012
